desc: Fault 205 candidate root cause (see evidence/2026-10-29-gravitylinux-survey.md). 5012 found a secondaries-only write denial over a physical range near the ADT end but read only the legacy CTRR_A/B regs. M4 has a second CTRR instance, CTRR_C (s3_0_c11_c0_0/1, EL1 encodings), enabled on secondaries only; Asahi m1n1 a735ea2+442c7a2+00b8814 and Gravity eb6cab7 reserve it as an FDT mem-rsv, which with idle=nop+arm64.nowfxt makes M4/M4 Pro SMP reliable (Gravity runs all 16 CPUs on M4 Max). Step 1 offline: add the CTRR_C/D/CTXR names from Asahi 442c7a2 to our proxyclient apple_regs.json and t6040-cpu-sysreg-diff.py; cherry-pick a735ea2+00b8814 into the m1n1 fork (keep From: authors). Step 2 rig, reads only: dump CTRR_C/D LWR/UPR/CTL per core and overlay on the 5012 v3 AT bitmap (Asahi says 48 KiB; 5012 saw >256 KiB, explain the gap). Step 3 rig: 217 cow reproducer at maxcpus=2 then 6 with the reservation m1n1; PASS = no 205 fault over the run matrix. Do not drop maxcpus=1 from the daily image until 4000 matrix passes. UPDATE 2026-10-30 (evidence/2026-10-30-t6040-5015-ctrr-macos-abstract-and-live-layout.md): macOS writes no CTRR reg on any CPU, so the window is firmware-locked and a carve-out is the only remedy; macOS reads [3,0,11,1,2/3] with UPR inclusive (last byte UPR+0xfff), so Asahi ALIGN_UP(UPR) is a page short when UPR is aligned. Live boot: m1n1 80badc91 has no CTRR mem-rsv; [adt_end, m1n1 _base) = 384 KiB of allocatable RAM covers 5012s denial. Step 2 now reads [3,0,11,0,0..3], [3,0,11,1,0..5] on the boot CPU AND one secondary, UPR inclusive, overlaid on [adt_end-16K, adt_end+0x60000). Step 3 runs two variants: (a) the Asahi series as-is, (b) a Wallace m1n1 mem-rsv over [adt_end, m1n1 _base); both cmdlines add arm64.nowfxt (CPU has FEAT_WFxT; flokli-code.patch with idle=nop skips WFIT but __delay still loops on WFET). CORRECTION 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 5495c18): variant (b) reserves the FIXED span [adt_end, adt_end+0x60000), using m1n1 _base only if it equals adt_end+0x60000 (else warn and keep the fixed span), because after a chainload the running stage can sit elsewhere. UPR: if its low 12 bits are zero, the exclusive end = UPR+0x1000 rounded up to 16K and Asahi ALIGN_UP is a page short; if UPR ends in 0xfff, Asahi is right; record which case. Step 3 pass criterion: log any fault OUTSIDE the reserved span (the 2026-07-29 maxcpus=14 boot faulted again about 7.9 MiB above adt_end); one means a second mechanism. The no-IMPDEF/TLBI finding covers the early boot text only. CENSUS 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex ac71e08): no CTRR self-write anywhere in the macOS kernel, no s3_0_c15 (chicken) writes; the per-CPU-init caveat is closed except whether SPRR/GXF state differs between boot CPU and secondaries (only relevant if step 3 still faults). BLOCKER for steps 1 and 3: the enrolled m1n1 source 80badc91 is not on GitHub (NEXT_STEPS manual command 2b). HYPOTHESIS 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 782a58c, unverified, needs the ADT): the July-29 second fault (PA 0x10006724f90, adt_end+0x7d8f90, outside the 384 KiB carve-out) could be a preloaded firmware-protected range (ANE segment-ranges or similar for other coprocessors) that Linux was allowed to allocate, rather than CTRR_C. Counterpoint: today the kernel CMA sits at 0x10005000000..0x10006ffffff, which would contain that PA on a similar layout, so it may just be a cascade page. Once the ADT is available, compare every segment-ranges or pre-loaded region with that PA and with live /proc/iomem; any such range that is not reserved is a bug on its own. PARITY 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 83c6870; only if 205 survives the reservation): macOS starts a secondary with plain 32-bit writes to PMGR reg[0]+0x88000: +0x4 = packed mask of started cores, +0x8+4*c = per-cluster core mask for every cluster (0 for clusters not started), stop = +0x0; entry PA 0, no reset-vector write, no readback, only dsb sy x2 before, and no protection state anywhere in the path. The +0x4 bit position comes from the PMGR ADT clusters table (u16 ncores, u16 bitpos per cluster). m1n1 main (16b1f61, src/smp.c:161/164; CHECK 80badc91 once pushed) writes +0x4 = 1 << (4*cluster + core) and +0x8+4*cluster = 1 << core (a single core, not a running mask). On J614s (4E+5P+5P, live DT cpu@0..3, cpu@10100..10104, cpu@10200..10204) cluster 1 core 4 (bit 8) aliases cluster 2 core 0 (bit 8). All 14 cores start, so this is not a start failure and not a known 205 mechanism; compare with the ADT clusters table. Per-CPU sysregs XNU sets on every secondary start/wake that m1n1 leaves alone or sets differently: s3_4_c15_c14_6 (AGTCNTRDIR_EL12) = 3 (m1n1 0); ACTLR_EL1 bits [11:9] cleared; s3_4_c15_c9_6 |= (index<<4)|0xf (timebase event stream, unset by m1n1). Parity only; none looks like memory protection. CORRECTIONS 2026-10-30 (wallace-rex 28d50d9): the s3_0_c11 census is 18 guest (_EL12) encodings, not 20 (conclusion unchanged). The per-cluster mask vs one-core-per-start difference at +0x8+4*c is equivalent under write-1-to-act; the only parity item is the +0x4 bit-8 collision. BUILT 2026-10-31 (on the M4, evidence/2026-10-31-t6040-5015-m1n1-reservation-objects.md): m1n1 80badc91 is now on damsleth/m1n1 main (PR #1), patches 0001-0004 apply cleanly; 0005 (reserve RTBuddySeg/SEPFW/SEPPatches/uStuff/preoslog/BootArgs) and 0006 (start bit from the PMGR clusters table, optional) added. Three standalone objects = the 5019 object with only m1n1 swapped, built twice identical, strict verify and preflight OK, NOT booted: 5015a (0001-0004) 622e8de1, 5015b (0001-0005) 074fa8bc, 5015c (0001-0006) b66f3493. gcc 12.2 native build, not byte-comparable to the Mac-built enrolled m1n1 bf4b2462 (flags not recorded). Boot check for B is 5030; step 2 should also read CTRR_D and, on a parked secondary, SIQ_CFG_EL1, s3_1_c15_c7_4 and s3_5_c15_c6_2 (WFI power-down hypothesis, wallace-rex 94ea32e/c37b6f0). The July-29 second fault is a permission fault (CTRR signature), so C and D bounds are the lead, with the SEP chain as hygiene. HOW TO READ (step 2, rig, read-only, over the chainloaded m1n1 via scripts/t6040-run-sysreg-diff.sh): SYSREG_ARGS="--ctrr" reads CTRR_C/D LWR/UPR/CTL on cpu0, cpu1, cpu5; SYSREG_ARGS="--idle" reads the WFI power-down state (SIQ_CFG_EL1, s3_4_c15_c14_6, s3_4_c15_c9_6, s3_1_c15_c7_4, s3_5_c15_c6_2, deep-sleep arm last). Log D bounds next to the m1n1 base on the same boot: the 07-29 second fault may sit under CTRR_D. REVISION 2026-10-31 (independent review of 0004-0006): ADT_GETPROP_ARRAY over-copies before its length check (latent, not reachable with J614s data). New patch 0007 fixes the TrustCache and chain reads with a length-first helper; 0006 gained a bit>=32 guard. Series order: 0001-0005, 0007, optionally 0006. Objects rebuilt (each built twice identical, strict verify and preflight OK, not booted): 5015b (0001-0005,0007) b1b550f3, 5015c (+0006) 9bee06be. The earlier 5015a/b/c (622e8de1, 074fa8bc, b66f3493) are superseded and moved to /mnt/sd/superseded-20261031/.

note: 2026-10-31 ADT READOUT (j614s 2026-07-28 dump, offline, unconfirmed on rig): /chosen/memory-map has an entry 'TrustCache' at exactly [adt_end, adt_end + 0x60000), followed by the booted image (m1n1 + payload). So the 384 KiB unreserved gap where every first fault lands is iBoot's static trust cache region, and the 5012 secondary-only deny window lies inside it. Fits a CTRR range that covers the trust cache. Fix direction unchanged (reserve, don't unlock), with a third carve-out variant: m1n1 reserves the memory-map 'TrustCache' range by name instead of adt_end arithmetic. Step 2 prediction: CTRR_C LWR/UPR on a secondary bound a subset of [TrustCache start - 1 ADT page, TrustCache end). The second fault (0x10006724f90, 2026-07-29) is not in any fixed firmware range; it needs the live ADT of a faulting boot (5027). | 2026-10-31 OFFLINE: the third carve-out variant is written as patches/m1n1-ctrr-c-v1/0004 (reserve memory-map TrustCache by name, inside the 0001 M4+ gate; AI-written, local fork only, never upstream). Syntax-checked only. Step 3 run matrix should use 0001-0004 together; the step 2 CTRR_C read then says whether 0001 alone would have been enough. Review: evidence/2026-10-31-review-5015-0004-codex.md.
